title: Tinyfloat oddities — bughunt notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal log of experiments and breadcrumbs while chasing intermittent quality regressions and NaN spikes when running tinyfloat formats (FP8/INT8 mixed) on A100 pools. The goal: capture commands, hypotheses, what I tried and short outcomes so I can hand off to SRE/quant team if needed.

Summary of problem observed:
- Intermittent NaN tokens produced in streaming generation for long-context chat workload (seq_len ~ 8k) after ~600 tokens in ~3% of requests.
- Repro mainly when using FP8 (E4M3-like) with per-tensor scaling + fused-layernorm on serving runtime.
- Switching those endpoints to BF16 eliminates NaNs but increases GPU memory and cost.

Environment snapshot:
- Model: open-redwood/rrr-7b-v2 (Transformer-blocks with rotary embeddings)
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (driver 525.85), CUDA 11.8
- Runtime: redwood-serving-runtime v2.9.1 (container image sha: 7a2f3b)
- PyTorch: internal fork ~1.13.1+ropt
- Kernel: custom fused attention + KV cache optimizations; fused GeLU and fused RMSLayerNorm variants present

Repro attempts (commands run):
1) Baseline reproduce (fast):
   export RWQ_LOG_LEVEL=debug
   python run_inference.py --model rrr-7b-v2 --quant fp8 --scale per_tensor --fused_layernorm true --seq_len 8192 --streams 16 --seed 42 2>&1 | tee run.fp8.baseline.log
   Observed: ~3/100 runs contain 'loss=nan' in internal eval harness.

2) Disable fused layernorm:
   python run_inference.py --quant fp8 --fused_layernorm false --other-flags
   Observed: NaNs disappeared in local 50-run loop. Strong hint: LN fusion interaction with quant path.

3) Per-channel scaling test:
   python run_inference.py --quant fp8 --scale per_channel
   Observed: Significant reduction of NaNs but not fully eliminated (~0.4%). Per-channel floats are heavier but more robust.

4) BF16 fallback for LayerNorm only (hybrid):
   export RWQ_LAYERNORM_FP=bf16
   python run_inference.py --quant fp8
   Observed: No NaNs in 200-run smoke. Latency ~+2.3%. Promising mitigation.

5) Stochastic rounding vs nearest:
   python run_inference.py --quant fp8 --rounding stochastic
   Observed: Variance in outputs increased; NaN rate down slightly. Not ideal for determinism.

6) Longer context stress test on dedicated node using 64 streams (to hit batching / kv collisions):
   ./stress_qps.sh --model rrr-7b-v2 --quant fp8 --streams 64 --time 2h
   Observed: After ~45m, two nodes reported CUDA kernel errors and then NaN propagation. Logs attached below.

Error snippets / logs (copied here):
- internal eval log line:
  2025-01-24 13:12:02,841 WARN eval-worker: step 617: loss=nan, tokens_generated=612

- python tensor dump (after generate returned):
  >>> torch.isnan(out).any()
  tensor(True)
  >>> out[0, -8:]
  tensor([nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan], device='cuda:0')

- CUDA kernel trace (snippet):
  [E cuda] driver: kernel launch failed: invalid configuration
  [E cuda] last_cuda_error: 59 (device-side assert triggered)

Immediate hypotheses (ordered):
1) Accumulated quantization error in attention softmax/exp leading to Inf -> NaN after softmax normalization under long contexts.
2) LayerNorm fusions assume FP32 intermediate accumulators; with FP8 end-to-end the small denominators produce divide-by-zero or denormal that becomes NaN in custom kernel.
3) Per-tensor scale is too coarse for some heads/layers; overflow in matmul accumulation triggers Inf which propagates.
4) A scheduling bug in fused KV cache path under high concurrency causes memory corruption occasionally (less likely given reproducibility with layernorm toggles).

What I tried to validate each hypothesis:
- Hypothesis (1): instrumented attention softmax with max clamp and added small eps to denom before softmax. Command:
  export RWQ_SOFTMAX_EPS=1e-6
  rerun baseline -> NaNs reduced but not gone. Suggests softmax contributes but not sole cause.

- Hypothesis (2): forced LayerNorm op to use float32 accumulators inside fused kernel (compile flag RWQ_LN_ACC_FP32=1). Result: NaNs eliminated in 400-run test. Strong signal.

- Hypothesis (3): switched to per-channel scales -> partial fix as noted. Also tried increasing scale bitwidth (simulate by storing scale in FP16) and this reduced incidents.

- Hypothesis (4): ran ASAN-like memory checks on kernel (hard to do on prod). On single-node dev with reduced batch, no memory corruption observed. Low probability right now.

Short-term mitigations we can deploy quickly:
- Feature-flag endpoints to use BF16 for LayerNorm (RWQ_LAYERNORM_FP=bf16) — low perf cost, big reliability win.
- Use per-channel scaling for FP8 on models with long context by default (config override).
- Add softmax eps clamp configurable (RWQ_SOFTMAX_EPS) with conservative default 1e-6.

Longer-term engineering items:
- Revisit fused LayerNorm kernels: ensure accumulation in at least FP16/FP32 and include explicit denormal handling and clamp. Unit test coverage across long contexts and different attention score magnitudes.
- Add model-aware quantization calibration: detect attention head variance and adapt per-channel scales during offline quant.
- Instrumentation: add histogram logs of pre-softmax logits, layernorm variance, and scale ratios per layer to surface hotspots in prod.
- Consider automatic hybrid precision planner: select per-op fallback precision (e.g., layernorm/softmax/gelu) based on observed numerics.

Next steps for me (todo):
- [ ] Prepare a small repro that toggles only fused-LN compile flag and run through perf/regression harness (deadline 2025-02-05).
- [ ] File a focused PR with simple guarded change: accumulation in LN kernel -> fp32 and a small eps in denom. Link to this doc.
- [ ] Add a dashboard metric: count of requests with any GPU NaN occurrences per model-version. (talk to Avery on observability).
- [ ] Collate representative tensor dumps + seed + request payload for infra team to repro on Dedicated cluster.

Notes / misc observations:
- Increasing temperature in generation sometimes delays NaN onset (weird). Could be because logits distribution spreads and avoids sharp peaks that trigger overflow?
- Reproduced similar symptom once with INT8 matmul path (non-fp8) but that was resolved by switching to per-channel scales there too.
- Determinism: stochastic rounding reduced NaNs but makes debugging harder; prefer deterministic fixes first.

Attachments / quick pointers (local):
- run.fp8.baseline.log (in my workspace)
- fast-repro.zip (scripts + minimal request payloads) -> github link in linked_artifacts

If handing off: include the following in the ticket/context: exact container sha, the exported env flags used, and the short list of configs that fixed the issue (LN->bf16 or LN accum->fp32).

End of note. Will iterate if I find a smaller repro or a kernel-level trace.
